chunks.title: SORYU company reference
chunks.text: SORYU SYSTEMS is the in-app organization. Its existing morph-ai PostgreSQL database is the authoritative source for employees, departments, clients, products, delivery work and client interactions. This reference does not establish legal corporate facts, revenue, contractual commitments or employee achievements.

chunks.title: SORYU company reference
chunks.text: The recorded products are Soryu CloudOps, Soryu Insight, Soryu Flow and Soryu Guard. Product-specific reference documents quote their verified database descriptions. Client adoption is related through client_products and product_usage; contracts relate a client/product subscription to a recorded contract owner.

chunks.title: SORYU company reference
chunks.text: Use live records for status, owner, due date and usage values. Authored reference documents explain the data model. Procedures marked proposed are recommendations awaiting company approval. A count in a bounded response describes the visible result set, not necessarily the entire business.

chunks.title: Organization and reporting model
chunks.text: employees.department_id references departments.id. employees.manager_id references employees.id. The seven named departments supplied for this project are Engineering, Customer Success, Product, Sales, Support, Operations and Data & Analytics. Look up actual membership rather than inferring it from a job title.

chunks.title: Organization and reporting model
chunks.text: A manager link identifies a recorded reporting relationship. It does not prove incident authority, approval rights or current availability. A missing manager is reported as missing. Cycles and absent records terminate traversal instead of manufacturing a hierarchy.

chunks.title: Organization and reporting model
chunks.text: Start a delivery question with the recorded work owner. If escalation is needed, offer the recorded manager as a possible contact, explicitly as a proposed action. Do not claim that the manager caused or can resolve a blocker.

chunks.title: Responsibilities and ownership conventions
chunks.text: Projects, tasks and issues use owner_employee_id. Meetings use organizer_employee_id. Contracts use contract_owner_id. Clients use account_manager_id. These foreign keys take precedence over legacy textual owner labels. The browser cannot choose the authenticated employee ID, role or department.

chunks.title: Responsibilities and ownership conventions
chunks.text: tasks.blocker_task_id points to a recorded prerequisite task. It is evidence of a dependency, not evidence of fault. Resolve the blocking task and its owner separately, including the case where the prerequisite is already completed.

chunks.title: Responsibilities and ownership conventions
chunks.text: No recorded owner means unknown ownership. Do not substitute a department head, meeting attendee, communication author or similarly named person. Proposed handoffs must identify an intended target and await a separately authorized write workflow.

chunks.title: Cross-department collaboration model
chunks.text: Engineering investigates implementation failures; Support coordinates incident triage; Customer Success brings client context; Product prioritizes trade-offs; Sales checks contract ownership; Operations coordinates schedules; Data & Analytics verifies measurement definitions. These responsibilities are a proposed operating model, not newly recorded assignments.

chunks.title: Cross-department collaboration model
chunks.text: Attach the source task or issue ID, known status, client/product/project links, current owner and explicit uncertainty. Ask the receiving owner to acknowledge the request. A communication record is evidence that a message exists, not proof that responsibility changed.

chunks.title: Cross-department collaboration model
chunks.text: Use recorded owners and managers for contact suggestions. Leave commitments, deadlines and staffing changes unchanged until an authorized company workflow approves them.

chunks.title: Record and evidence terminology
chunks.text: A recorded field value, such as projects.status = Delayed, is an observation. Its evidence includes the exact row and field. It does not automatically explain why the status occurred.

chunks.title: Record and evidence terminology
chunks.text: An aggregate or comparison is a calculation over named source records and a documented date window. Daily active users can be averaged by measured day; summing them does not yield unique users. Missing measurements remain missing, not zero.

chunks.title: Record and evidence terminology
chunks.text: An unverified cause is uncertainty. A procedure or next step is a proposed action, not a historical fact. Recorded issue detail is reported as a source's description, never independently verified causation.

chunks.title: Record and evidence terminology
chunks.text: retrieved_at records when live evidence was read. Document version and heading identify reference material. Entity navigation is an internal descriptor resolved through authenticated APIs, not a fabricated URL. Generated briefs are snapshots, never authoritative updates.

chunks.title: Engineering operating reference

chunks.title: Engineering operating reference
chunks.text: Relevant records include project tasks, assigned issues and technical activity events. Actual employees are selected by employees.department_id. Their tasks and issues follow owner_employee_id; project ownership is a separate relationship and must not be inferred from task counts.

chunks.title: Engineering operating reference
chunks.text: Coordinate with Support for reproducible incident evidence; Product for prioritization; Operations for change windows. Shared client_id, product_id and project_id relationships provide context, not implicit reassignment.

chunks.title: Engineering operating reference

chunks.text: Resolve client ID and the requested meeting date. If more than one client matches, ask the employee to choose.

chunks.title: Client meeting preparation

chunks.title: Client meeting preparation

chunks.title: Client meeting preparation
